title: Medical Imaging Systems
description: Engineering principles of X-ray, CT, ultrasound, MRI and nuclear imaging systems, image quality, digital imaging and PACS, and equipment maintenance.

topics.title: X-ray Systems Engineering
topics.summary: X-ray tube design, high-voltage generators, detectors and digital radiography.

notes.b: An X-ray tube is an evacuated glass or metal envelope containing a heated tungsten filament cathode (thermionic emission — tube current mA set by filament heating) and a tungsten (or tungsten–rhenium; molybdenum for mammography) anode target. Electrons accelerated by the kilovoltage (kVp) strike the anode, producing bremsstrahlung and characteristic X-rays with only about 1% efficiency; 99% becomes heat. Rotating anodes spread heat over a larger area; the line-focus principle (anode angle) gives a small effective focal spot with a larger actual focal area. Heat units and tube rating charts limit exposures. High-frequency generators convert mains power to high-frequency AC before transformation and rectification, giving nearly constant potential (low ripple), smaller transformers and more consistent output than single- or three-phase generators. The automatic exposure control (AEC) terminates exposure when the detector reaches the preset dose.

Film-screen systems have been largely replaced by digital systems. Computed radiography (CR) uses photostimulable phosphor plates (barium fluorohalide) read by a laser scanner. Direct digital radiography (DR) uses flat-panel detectors: indirect conversion (scintillator such as caesium iodide converts X-rays to light, detected by amorphous silicon photodiodes/TFT array) or direct conversion (amorphous selenium converts X-rays directly to charge — higher spatial resolution, used in mammography). Performance metrics: detective quantum efficiency (DQE — how efficiently a detector uses incoming X-ray quanta), modulation transfer function (MTF — spatial resolution), dynamic range and noise. Anti-scatter grids improve contrast by absorbing scattered radiation. Fluoroscopy systems use image intensifiers or flat-panel detectors for real-time imaging.

topics.title: Computed Tomography Systems
topics.summary: Gantry components, detectors, reconstruction algorithms and CT performance testing.

notes.b: A CT gantry contains the X-ray tube (high heat capacity), high-voltage generator, collimators, bow-tie filter (shapes beam intensity across the patient), a curved array of detectors (solid-state ceramic scintillators with photodiodes), a data acquisition system (DAS) that digitises signals, and slip rings transmitting power and data during continuous rotation (rotation times < 0.3 s in modern scanners). Multidetector rows provide wide z-axis coverage; dual-energy CT uses two energy spectra (dual-source, rapid kV switching or layered detectors) for material decomposition. Photon-counting detectors (cadmium telluride) directly count individual photons and their energies, improving resolution and dose efficiency.

Image reconstruction converts projection data (sinogram) into images. Filtered back projection (FBP) is fast but noisy at low dose; iterative reconstruction models noise and system physics to reduce noise and dose; deep-learning reconstruction is increasingly used. The Radon transform underlies the mathematics. CT quality assurance uses phantoms to test CT number accuracy (water 0 ± 5 HU) and uniformity, noise, low-contrast detectability, spatial resolution (line pairs, MTF), slice thickness and dose (CTDI measured with a pencil ionisation chamber in PMMA head/body phantoms). Daily air calibration and water phantom checks detect detector problems (ring artefacts).

topics.title: Ultrasound and MRI Instrumentation
topics.summary: Transducer construction, beamforming, MRI magnets, gradients, RF systems and siting.

notes.b: Ultrasound transducers use piezoelectric elements (lead zirconate titanate, PZT, or single crystals) with a backing (damping) layer to shorten pulses and improve axial resolution, and a matching layer (thickness a quarter wavelength) to reduce impedance mismatch with skin. Array transducers (linear, curvilinear, phased) steer and focus beams electronically by timing (delays) applied to elements — beamforming, increasingly digital and software-based. The system transmits pulses, receives echoes, applies time-gain compensation, demodulates, performs log compression and scan conversion for display. Doppler processing uses quadrature detection and autocorrelation (colour) or FFT (spectral). Maintenance: check cables and lenses for cracks, test with tissue-mimicking phantoms for resolution, depth and dead elements.

MRI hardware: the main magnet (superconducting niobium–titanium coils in liquid helium at about 4 K; permanent or resistive magnets in low-field open systems), shim coils (improve field homogeneity), gradient coils (x, y, z — rapidly switched by powerful amplifiers, producing noise and eddy currents), radiofrequency transmit and receive coils (including phased-array surface coils), and the RF shielded room (Faraday cage — copper lining to exclude external RF interference). Cryogen management uses cold heads and compressors (zero-boil-off systems); helium supply and power stability are major challenges in Nigeria, where frequent power failures can cause quenches. Siting considerations include the fringe field (5-gauss line — limit for pacemakers), floor loading, vibration, and quench pipes venting outside.

topics.title: Nuclear Medicine Instrumentation
topics.summary: Gamma cameras, SPECT, PET and radiopharmaceutical production equipment.

notes.b: The gamma (Anger) camera detects gamma rays emitted from radiopharmaceuticals in the patient. Components: collimator (lead with holes — parallel-hole, pinhole, converging/diverging — determines resolution and sensitivity; only photons travelling in specific directions pass), a large sodium iodide crystal doped with thallium (NaI(Tl)) that scintillates, an array of photomultiplier tubes converting light to electrical signals, positioning logic (Anger logic) and pulse height analyser (energy window, e.g. 140 keV ± 10% for technetium-99m — rejects scatter). SPECT (single-photon emission computed tomography) rotates camera heads around the patient to reconstruct 3D images; SPECT/CT adds attenuation correction and anatomical localisation. Technetium-99m (half-life 6 hours, 140 keV gamma) from molybdenum-99 generators is the workhorse isotope.

Positron emission tomography detects pairs of 511 keV annihilation photons emitted in opposite directions when a positron meets an electron; coincidence detection by a ring of detectors (e.g. LSO/LYSO or BGO crystals) defines a line of response without needing a collimator, giving higher sensitivity. Time-of-flight PET improves localisation. The main tracer is fluorine-18 fluorodeoxyglucose (FDG, half-life 110 minutes), produced in a cyclotron and synthesised in automated modules within shielded hot cells; it maps glucose metabolism in cancers, brain and heart. PET/CT and PET/MRI combine function and anatomy. Quality control: daily uniformity (flood) checks, energy peaking, centre of rotation for SPECT, dose calibrator constancy and accuracy checks. Nigeria has few nuclear medicine centres (e.g. Ibadan, Lagos, Abuja).

topics.title: Digital Imaging, PACS and Equipment Management
topics.summary: DICOM, PACS/RIS, image processing, AI tools, and maintenance of imaging equipment.

notes.b: Digital images consist of pixels (2D) or voxels (3D) with bit depth determining the number of grey levels (e.g. 12 bits = 4,096 levels). DICOM (Digital Imaging and Communications in Medicine) is the standard for storing and transmitting medical images and metadata between modalities and systems. PACS (Picture Archiving and Communication System) stores and distributes images; RIS (Radiology Information System) manages scheduling, reports and billing; HL7 messaging links RIS with the hospital information system. Teleradiology sends images for remote reporting — valuable in Nigeria given the shortage of radiologists. Image processing includes windowing, filtering (smoothing, edge enhancement), segmentation and 3D rendering (MPR, MIP, volume rendering). AI tools assist with detection (e.g. TB on chest X-ray — CAD4TB used in Nigerian TB programmes) and triage.

Healthcare technology management covers needs assessment, procurement (specifications, compatibility, service contracts, training, spare parts), installation and acceptance testing, user training, preventive maintenance (scheduled checks), corrective maintenance (repairs), performance testing and calibration, and decommissioning. Much imaging equipment in Nigerian hospitals is non-functional due to poor maintenance, lack of spare parts, unstable power (use of voltage stabilisers, UPS and dedicated generators), and inadequate technical staff. Radiation equipment must comply with regulations of the Nigerian Nuclear Regulatory Authority (NNRA), including licensing, shielding assessment and periodic QA. A computerised maintenance management system (CMMS) tracks inventory, work orders and maintenance schedules.
